formats.label: La Pilule de Culture G
formats.title: Quatre-vingt-dix-sept : la France a un problème de calcul
formats.tagline: Pourquoi on compte « quatre fois vingt » en France, et pas en Belgique

cast.look: Sofie, a modern Belgian tourist in her thirties, short blond bob, black raincoat, a red umbrella as the only colour
Marc, a modern Parisian café waiter, tall and lanky, slicked black hair, thin moustache, white shirt, black waistcoat, long white apron
Gautier, a 13th-century Parisian cloth merchant, round belly, bowl haircut, grey tunic with a black belt, a small purse at his waist, counting on his fingers
Claude, a pompous 17th-century grammarian, enormous curly black wig, pointy little moustache, black coat with a huge white lace collar, nose in the air, holding a thick book

cover.prompt: a small café table. Sofie (on the left) holding a restaurant bill, counting desperately on all ten fingers, eyes crossed; Marc (on the right) standing with a tray, smiling politely, waiting. medium shot

cases.caption: En France, 97 se dit « quatre-vingt-dix-sept » : quatre fois vingt, plus dix-sept.

image.prompt: a bare café with one small round table. Marc (on the right) handing over a bill with a polite smile; Sofie (on the left) sitting, staring at the bill, one eyebrow very high, pen frozen in the air. medium shot

cases.caption: Au Moyen Âge, on compte par vingtaines : « deux vins » pour 40, « trois vins » pour 60.

bubbles.text: Ce drap vaut trois vins deniers.

image.prompt: a simple medieval market stall with one roll of grey cloth. Gautier (on the left) counting proudly on his fingers in groups; Marc (on the right), out of place in his waiter apron, pulling his own hair in frustration. medium shot

cases.caption: Saint Louis fonde à Paris l’hospice des Quinze-Vingts : 300 lits, soit quinze fois vingt.

bubbles.text: Le nom est resté : l’hôpital existe toujours.

image.prompt: a long bare hall with many identical small beds in a row disappearing into the distance. Gautier (on the left) proudly pointing down the row; Marc (on the right) trying to count the beds one by one with his finger, dizzy. wide shot

cases.caption: D’où vient ce système ? Peut-être des Celtes, peut-être des Normands. Personne n’en est sûr.

bubbles.text: Mon grand-père comptait comme ça. Et le sien.

image.prompt: Gautier (on the left) shrugging with both palms up, totally unbothered; Marc (on the right) leaning forward with a notebook, eager, then deflating. plain background. medium shot

cases.caption: Trente, quarante, cinquante et soixante finissent par s’imposer.

bubbles.text: Adieu, « trois vins ». Tu étais si joli.

image.prompt: Gautier (in the middle) sitting alone on his market stool, slumped, a single tear rolling down, holding his ten fingers up sadly. plain background. close-up

cases.caption: Mais sous l’influence de Vaugelas, l’Académie retient soixante-dix, quatre-vingts et quatre-vingt-dix.

image.prompt: a bare salon with one gilded chair. Claude (on the left) nose in the air, waving a lace handkerchief in disgust; Marc (on the right) holding his notepad, mouth open in disbelief. medium shot

cases.caption: En Belgique et en Suisse, septante et nonante sont officiels. En Suisse, on dit même huitante.

bubbles.text: Nous, on compte par dizaines. Comme pour soixante.

image.prompt: Sofie (on the left) calmly counting on her fingers in neat groups, relaxed smile, red umbrella under her arm; Claude (on the right) fainting backwards dramatically, wig sliding off, the back of his hand on his forehead. plain background. medium shot

cases.caption: Septante reste au dictionnaire. En France, il n’est pas interdit : juste « vieilli ».

image.prompt: Sofie (in the middle) in a confession-style close-up, looking straight at the reader with a satisfied little smile, holding up seven fingers. plain background

final.text: « Quatre-vingts » est un vestige du comptage par vingt du Moyen Âge ; l’hospice parisien des Quinze-Vingts comptait 300 lits.

sources.title: Académie française — Questions de langue : soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix

formats.label: L’Insolite Historique
formats.title: La Marseillaise est née à Strasbourg (Marseille n’a fait que chanter)
formats.tagline: Écrite en une nuit pour l’armée du Rhin, elle doit son nom à des volontaires qui passaient par là

cast.look: Claude-Joseph, a young 1790s army engineer captain, curly powdered hair tied back, eager face, black uniform coat with a red collar as the only colour, holding a violin
Philippe-Frédéric, the mayor of Strasbourg in 1792, plump and jovial, white powdered wig, rosy cheeks, black coat, a wide black sash
a 1792 volunteer from Marseille, sunburnt, big black moustache, broad grin, white shirt, black trousers, a red bonnet as the only colour, a musket on his shoulder

cover.prompt: a long road. a column of singing volunteers marching in the background. the volunteer (on the right, in front) singing at full lungs, chest out; Claude-Joseph (on the left) running after them waving his violin, shouting, sweating. wide shot

cases.caption: Strasbourg. La France vient de déclarer la guerre. On se réunit chez le maire, Dietrich.

bubbles.text: Il nous faudrait un chant pour l’armée !
Je suis ingénieur. Mais j’ai un violon.

image.prompt: a bare dining room with one table and a candelabra. Philippe-Frédéric (on the right) raising a glass enthusiastically; Claude-Joseph (on the left) shyly lifting his violin from under the table, blushing. medium shot

cases.caption: Le capitaine Rouget de Lisle l’écrit dans la nuit du 25 au 26 avril.

bubbles.text: Allons enfants… de la… de la quoi, déjà ?

image.prompt: a small room at night lit by one candle. Claude-Joseph (in the middle) sitting at a desk covered in crumpled papers, hair standing up, violin under his chin, writing with a quill at the same time, wild inspired eyes. medium shot

cases.caption: Son titre : « Chant de guerre pour l’armée du Rhin ». Pas un mot sur Marseille.

image.prompt: Philippe-Frédéric (on the right) holding up a sheet of music with both hands like a trophy, tearful with pride; Claude-Joseph (on the left) exhausted, dark circles, slumped against the wall, giving a weak thumbs up. plain background. medium shot

cases.caption: Le chant voyage jusqu’à Marseille. Des volontaires l’emportent en montant vers Paris.

bubbles.text: Ça se chante super bien en marchant, ce truc !

image.prompt: an empty sunny road with a single milestone. the volunteer (on the right) marching with a huge grin, singing with his mouth wide open, musket on his shoulder, a crumpled music sheet sticking out of his pocket. tiny marching silhouettes behind him. wide shot

cases.caption: Ils entrent dans Paris en le chantant. Les Parisiens l’appellent l’hymne des Marseillais.

bubbles.text: Euh… c’est moi qui l’ai écrite.

image.prompt: a Paris street full of tiny cheering silhouettes throwing hats in the air. the volunteer (on the right) waving to the crowd like a star; Claude-Joseph (on the left) squeezed in the corner, raising a small finger, totally ignored. wide shot

cases.caption: Elle devient chant national. Puis elle est interdite sous l’Empire et la Restauration.

image.prompt: Claude-Joseph (in the middle) holding his violin with a big black cross painted over a music sheet pinned on the wall behind him, jaw dropped, melting in despair, arms dangling. plain background. medium shot

cases.caption: La IIIe République en fait l’hymne national. Et le nom de Marseille est resté.

bubbles.text: Écrite à Strasbourg. Mais d’accord. Pas de souci.

image.prompt: Claude-Joseph (in the middle) in a confession-style close-up, looking straight at the reader with a very forced smile and one twitching eye, clutching his violin. plain background

final.text: La Marseillaise est née à Strasbourg, sous la plume de Rouget de Lisle, en avril 1792 ; elle est hymne national depuis 1879.

sources.title: Élysée — La Marseillaise de Rouget de Lisle
Paris ZigZag — Pourquoi la Marseillaise s’appelle-t-elle ainsi ?
